Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the English players can be seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra to open the innings for New Zealand, which means Will Young is pushed down to number 3. Jofra Archer will get proceedings underway with the new ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Now then, 223 is another moderate total to chase down but there is plenty on offer for the pacers early on and New Zealand haven't been at their best with the bat either. Jofra Archer will be key for England if they are to have a chance of avoiding a whitewash. It should be an interesting run chase to say the least, so stick around as we aren't that far away from the second innings.

England will be grateful for their lower middle order, as at one point, even surpassing the 100-run mark seemed like a steep ask. The top order failed miserably yet again and all across the three matches, England's top 4 has accumulated a total of just 84 runs, which is the lowest ever by a top 4 in an ODI series of three matches or more, absolutely staggering. Unlike the first two matches, skipper Harry Brook couldn't bail his team out and it was Jos Buttler who sparked a fightback. However, England were 102 for 7 when he got out and needed a miracle. It did come in the form of Jamie Overton and Brydon Carse, who put on 58 runs. Overton went on to score a stellar 68 and took England to a somewhat defendable total of 222.

New Zealand opted to bowl first on a surface that had plenty of grass on it and neither Jacob Duffy nor Zakary Foulkes disappointed. The duo had the English top order huffing and puffing and had them reeling at 44/5 before we eventually saw a bit of resistance. It was then Blair Tickner who bowled a lovely spell and halted England's fightback with a couple of wickets. However, the Kiwis failed to clean up the English lower order and even though Tickner ended with 4 wickets, the hosts ended up conceding much more runs than anticipated at one point.

End of an epic fightback from Jamie Overton as England are yet again bowled out in this series, three times in a row now. A strong showing from the Kiwi pacers, which has been the norm throughout this ODI series and overall, New Zealand will be pretty happy with that first innings. As for England, it was another underwhelming day out with the bat and they will certainly have a long chat after the game about their approach.

PITCH REPORT - Frances Mackay is pitchside. She informs that the square boundaries measure 61 and 56 metres, while it stretches to 84 metres down the ground. Grant Elliott joins her, and he shares that the pitch has been under bad weather for a few days, and the surface still feels soft in patches, though it’s rock hard underneath. Mentions that there is a fair bit of grass covering, which should offer some seam movement early on. Believes that the pitch might play a little on the slower side. Informs that the average first-innings score here is around 270, with 296 being the average winning total, something England will certainly have their eye on.

English all-rounder, Jamie Overton is down for a chat. He says that he hasn't been able to contribute with the bat much in the past, but hopes that they can finish with a win. Reckons that they are a positive team but sometimes it is absorbing pressure and a few things haven't gone their way so far. Adds that they aren't out of form, it is just that they haven't managed to go on and get the big total.

Daryl Mitchell is up for a chat. Mentions that it is nice to win games for New Zealand. Says that it does a little bit in New Zealand in October, so it is about adapting. Shares that he loves playing for the country, and the personal matters do not matter much to him. Further says that England are a world-class team and credits his bowlers for the way they have contained them. Regarding the surface, he feels that it might do a bit early doors since it is early summer and there might be a bit of tennis ball kind of bounce. Reckons that it will be about navigating through that early phase and then making hay.

England's captain, Harry Brook cheekily says that he would like to win a toss in the near future. Mentions that they will look to go out there and play with freedom. Adds that it is all about being present with the bat and putting the pressure on the bowlers. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

The captain of New Zealand, Mitchell Santner believes that this is a good wicket, but it feels a bit soft and has a good grass covering. Informs that they have one change with Kane Williamson missing out due to a groin niggle and Devon Conway replacing him. Adds that they have the same composition as the last game, with four seamers and two spinners. Shares that it is a good place to be with guys coming in and stepping up straight away.

With the series already in their grasp, New Zealand will be eyeing a clean sweep as they take on a struggling England in the third and final ODI at the Sky Stadium in Wellington. The hosts have looked a class apart so far - organized, disciplined, and ruthless when it mattered, while the visitors have been searching for answers with both bat and ball. England’s top and middle order kept faltering again and again - they failed to build meaningful partnerships and simply offered too many gifts in the 15-40 over phase, leaving the bowlers with far too little to defend. New Zealand, meanwhile, have been far more cohesive - their seamers struck early and often, highlighted by Blair Tickner’s match-winning four-for in the second game that broke the back of England’s batting. Daryl Mitchell anchored the chase with composure and the lower-middle order completed the job with the kind of calm finish that suggests a side comfortable in home conditions. Rachin Ravindra has also been among the runs and Kane Williamson adds that balance in the middle order, while the all-round abilities of Michael Bracewell and Mitchell Santner have been key to their success. England still boasts firepower - their batting depth, including the likes of Joe Root, Jos Buttler, and the talented Jamie Smith at the top. However, no one has fired except for skipper Harry Brook, who also scored a magnificent century in the first game. The bowling variation looks strong on paper with Jofra Archer and Brydon Carse being effective in these conditions, but in practice, they have struggled to convert good starts and instead have been pushed onto the back foot in seaming conditions. Add to that the context: New Zealand arrived off a clean 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan at home, so they know how to dominate when everything clicks, while England came into this after losing a home series 2-1 to South Africa, a result that has exposed cracks in their 50-over setup. Given the momentum, home advantage, and sharper execution, the Kiwis look favourites to seal the series here, or will England change the scoreline and finish on a high? Let's find out together.
